quest.title: A Mother's Last Wish
quest.description: While traveling, you receive a sudden invitation from Alice. She hopes you and Paimon can help Durin fulfill a wish — one connected to his late mother, "M"...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x475, Mora x49200, Hero's Wit x6, Mystic Enhancement Ore x11

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, it's Durin!

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME} and Paimon? Ah, I'm sorry, I hope I didn't scare you...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... No, you didn't scare us, just... gave us a little surprise, hehe... Looks like you've gotten even more powerful now.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Hmm... I don't know, it just feels like it's gotten harder to control. I didn't mean to strike so hard. I'm so relieved you didn't get hurt.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's all good! We've had worse, hehe!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is the Abyssal power inside you acting up?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Ah, no, don't worry about that. It's been very stable ever since I got this body. Albedo made sure of that.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: What you saw just now is something that only started happening recently. Maybe I'm still acclimating or something. I'm sure it'll clear up over time.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Anyway, what brings you here? Did you need something?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, well...

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: The day that the writer and the watcher crossed paths was the day that the magic known as storytelling was born.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, um... she asked us to come.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Ms. Alice?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: You too? I guess I really do need to work on my impression... Well, never mind that. It's been too long, Mini Durin! And, please, that's Aunt Alice to you.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: #I have brought you and {NICKNAME} together here for a very important purpose! It has to do with your mom.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: My mom?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You mean "M"?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Indeed! Fairytale author extraordinaire, Anya "Marie" Andersdotter. See, I knew this would be right up your alley.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Now then. If you'll open the book, I will begin narrating.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Open the book)

talks.objective: Enter the world within the book

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Well? Did you manage to find them?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, what is this place? It reminds Paimon of Simulanka...

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: The two are indeed similar. Both worlds were built using the same magic, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aha, so it IS Alice!

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Hello, um... Aunt Alice.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Aw, no need to be shy. Just think of me as one of your mother's dearest friends.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You keep talking about "stories" and "magic"... What's this all about? Simulanka 2.0 or something?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Certainly not! Simulanka was a peerless masterpiece. Without the original author, it would be impossible to create a sequel. Even for me!

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: But you are right about one thing. Just like last time, I want to show you a work of magic that has to do with storytelling.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: What's this?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's the book we just saw...

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: This... is your mother's dying wish.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: My mother's dying wish... was a book?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Let me answer that with a question. What do you suppose would be a writer's greatest regret?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Have you ever read a book called The Little Witch and the Undying Fire?

choices.text: I have. But I'm not sure who wrote it.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: That's because it was the work of more than one person.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: It began as a little game at our tea parties. Each of us took turns writing the next part of the story.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: I wrote the first volume, then the other mages took their turns. M was tasked with writing the final volume and tying everything up.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: But by the time everyone had finished writing their parts, M had passed away... Ah, it was a terrible shame. A true tragedy.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Mm...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: And that is the answer to my question. A writer's greatest regret is to leave a story unfinished.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That makes sense.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: But all is not lost. I couldn't stand the doom and gloom of it all, so I went ahead and wrote an ending myself, on her behalf.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Then, what's this book?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: This is the answer your mother gave to the same question. In her eyes, this was her greatest regret.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: She made me promise that I would bring it to you, because she believed the only person who could resolve this regret... is you.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: So my mother's greatest regret... is another unfinished story?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Mmhmm... You could say that.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: And I guess resolving the regret means... finishing the story?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: That's one way to put it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is a straight answer too much to ask for...?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Her answer was quite the opposite of what I'd expected. But oh, how touching it was!

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: I'd love to tell you what she said, I really would. But that would spoil the plot, and we can't have that. Spoilers ruin everything!

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Oh...

choices.text: Fine, we'll make do with the breadcrumbs...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Just think of this task as... giving a story a much-needed ending. All I ask is that you do your best.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: ...I understand. But I only just started learning human script, and I don't have any writing experience at all...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Hahaha, relax. Why else do you think your dear aunt went and found you two such wonderful helpers?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: With their experience, you'll have so many story ideas you won't know what to do with them. So don't be shy to ask lots of questions.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! If it's to help Durin fulfill his mother's dying wish, then we're in!

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Aunt Alice, could I ask... What kind of story was my mother hoping to write?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Heh, I had a feeling this might come up — but that answer isn't mine to give. You'll have to find it yourself, here inside this book.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Mm...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't worry, we'll help you come up with loads of ideas.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, let's find a nice spot where we can settle in and read through this thing. We could even get some snacks too!

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Hahaha, the actual process might not be quite the walk in the park you're imagining, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why's that?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Because when M created this book, she borrowed my magic. In other words, it's not a book you can just pick up and read — it's a magical book!

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Its chapters are scattered through memories of the past. Gather them all, and the book will show you its secrets.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: So, where are we supposed to find these memories?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: M left a trail of clues for each unfinished chapter. Follow the hints, and you'll find them.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Oh, and when it comes to adding to the story yourselves, you'll need to use this...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And this is...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: This, my dear little Paimon, is the ink M left behind — infused with a little of my own magic, of course. If you're planning on writing something inside the book, you'll need it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How very magical...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: It's extremely precious, so be sure to use it sparingly. This is all that's left.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: So we need to search for the memories and keep an eye on how much ink we're using...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It just had to be a wild goose chase, didn't it...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Perhaps it's just another form of storytelling? M was ever so creative when it came to things like that.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Just think of it as a little challenge your mom left behind. Who knows, there could even be a mysterious prize at the end of it all...

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: I don't care about that... This was my mother's dying wish. Whatever it takes, I'll find a way.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And we're here to help!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup! With the two of us by your side, you'll be just fine!

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Okie-dokie, that should be pretty much all you need to know...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Ah, and once the story's complete, do let me have a little looksie, okay? I've read everything she ever wrote, so naturally, I can't miss this one.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How will we find you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... Most of the time, you're pretty hard to pin down.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Don't worry, I'll know when you're finished. Just wait for me to reach out.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Alright, off you go! I can't wait to hear how the story ends.

choices.text: It's hardly the first time you've strung us along like this.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Ah, well, you're missing out. It's a wonderful book.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, here we are again... Alice's magic really is incredible, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's take a look at this book.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right! Alice mentioned we should be on the lookout for clues.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Mm...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Unknown Voice
dialogues.text: A corner of repose for countless tales, watched over by the honor of knights. A place for stories to sleep, perchance to dream of ancient cities and the epics of ages past.

dialogues.speaker: Unknown Voice
dialogues.text: There, a witch once spent a sleepless night — and all to bring forth a story yet untold.

dialogues.speaker: Unknown Voice
dialogues.text: Find the place I speak of, for it is where the seeds of this story lie.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Was that a riddle? Where do you think this mysterious place could be...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Obviously, it's the Mondstadt Library.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, you... might actually be onto something! Guess that means we need to head back to Mondstadt?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: ...I had a feeling that's where we would be headed. After all, it's where my mother was from, and I bet it's where she wrote this story too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, that makes sense...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Still... I feel bad about dragging the two of you along on such a long journey.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry about it! We don't really have much going on right now, so we're all yours! C'mon, let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Back in the Mondstadt Library, huh? Talk about a trip down memory lane!

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: So, we're supposed to find "the seeds of the story," right? What do you think that means?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, we're in a library, so it's gotta be books, right? But seriously, there's so many here... How are we supposed to know which ones we need?

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Making a racket in a library... You should know better than that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Lisa! Oh, um... Sorry about that.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Now who do we have here... Ah, my golden-haired cutie, and my little horned cutie too.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Sorry, Miss Lisa. I know you taught me to be quiet in the library, but Paimon was just trying to help... Please don't be too hard on her.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Well, it has been far too long since we saw each other, so I suppose I can let it slide just this once...

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Back when he first arrived here. Poor Jean wasn't sure what to do with him, so I stepped in to lend a hand.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: I figured, if I can handle a boy raised by wolves, then teaching one who's part dragon should be a walk in the park.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nice! Sounds like Durin was welcomed with open arms!

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Why, of course! Now, let's save the reminiscing for another time. I'm sure you're here for a reason. Did you need to borrow some books?

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: It's kind of hard to explain... Maybe you could take a look at this?

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Oh?

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Ah, I see. These so-called "seeds of the story" must be the books that inspired its creation.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: That's just how it is with stories — they grow out of the tales that came before them. And that mage... I can almost picture her here, hundreds of years ago, scribbling away at one of these very desks.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: But, we don't know anything about this story. How are we supposed to figure out which books inspired it?

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: As it happens, just before I found you here, I was looking into something rather peculiar. One of the knights reported seeing some books that weren't listed anywhere in our catalog.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Stranger still, just as he went to reach out for them, the books vanished into thin air... and then a while later, while he was browsing through other shelves, there they were again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: S—Seriously?

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: That particular knight knows this library inside and out. I'd be very surprised if he was seeing things.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Something tells me these might just be the magical books you're after...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's very possible...

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: According to the report, there are three of these books in total. I'll be relying on you to track them down, cuties.

choices.text: Feels like we were here just yesterday.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: An experiment log? Looks like part of the title's been erased...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's something seriously suspicious about this book!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Second Strongest Spell in Existence (Do Not Show Klee)"...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... there's actually a book like that, right here in the Mondstadt Library? That title's just gonna make people even more curious...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, there's definitely something fishy about this one...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kinda looks like a poetry collection... But why is part of the title missing...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's see what Lisa makes of it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: W—Wait, did Klee write this one!? Should this even be here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We'd better show it to Lisa...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Let's hang onto this one for now. Could be one of the ones we're looking for.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's one of M's, after all...

talks.objective: Search for books not listed in the library catalog

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Well? Did you manage to find them?

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Well, would you look at that? Seems like these are the little troublemakers you're after, and all three just so happen to be forbidden texts. What kind of story requires reference material like that, I wonder...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: F—Forbidden texts... Y'know, the first time you mentioned that the library had a "restricted section," Paimon thought you were just trying to scare us. A—Are you saying... it actually exists?

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Not really something you should be poking your little nose into, is it, cutie?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhhh, sorry...

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Seeing as it was Ms. Alice who asked you to look for these books, I won't question the matter. But they'll need to be sealed away again once you're done, so don't forget to return them.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Don't worry, Miss Lisa, I won't forget.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Well then, that's all from me. After all that hard work, I think I've earned myself a nice cup of tea.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, we've gathered all the reference books. What's next?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Wait, look...

talks.objective: Enter the world within the book

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... We're actually inside the story!

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: This must be Aunt Alice's magic...

choices.text: That was the opening we just heard, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah...

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: A story... about me?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why don't we just... see where the story takes us? All we know is the beginning at this point.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Okay.

response.speaker: Narrator
response.text: And now, a golden-haired Traveler, a silvery sprite, and a dragon-born youth step onto the stage. What new chapter will their arrival bring?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, that came out of nowhere... was that the same voice we heard just now?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sounds like this story even has its own narrator.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... But why does it sound so familiar?

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Mmm, I've missed this. It's just like the stories my mother used to tell me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean... "M"? She used to tell you stories?

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Yeah... She loved it, back when she was still alive...

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Sorry, we should focus on what we're here to do. So, now that we're in the story... what's next?

response.speaker: Narrator
response.text: The dragon-youth wondered aloud. Yet all he could do was wait for the story to unfold.

response.speaker: Narrator
response.text: Of course, there's something to be said for helping it along. Perhaps a little exploration could prove fruitful.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, is that a hint?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's follow her suggestion for now.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Yeah, I agree.

choices.text: Sounds like the story is about Durin...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'd better keep looking...

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Hm, seems like there's still some missing. Why don't you try checking the other shelves?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This must be the dragon egg, right? Looks like it's gonna hatch any moment now...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So we've got... a dragon egg about to hatch, a witch who loves stories, and that evil dragon we heard about at the beginning. Yep, it all adds up.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: This... is my story, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure looks like it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, so how are we supposed to help the story along? It feels like all we can do right now is wait.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Apparently, it hadn't dawned on the group to look for a way to help the egg hatch faster...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohhh, right. We're at the point in the story where we're waiting for the baby dragon to hatch, so that has to happen before the story can continue...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And... how do we do that?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: With the flames at his command, perhaps the dragon-youth might be able to provide the egg with sufficient warmth...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!? You want us to... roast the dragon egg?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: The silvery sprite's surprise betrayed her lack of reading — for in countless tales, it is told that only by fire's embrace will a dragon's egg hatch swiftly.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph, you... kinda have a point there.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wanna give it a try, Durin?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Okay, I'll... see what I can do.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: At last, under the witch's expectant gaze, the little dragon broke free from its shell.

dialogues.speaker: Story-Witch
dialogues.text: No living being has ever decided the moment of its birth. You were no exception, my child.

dialogues.speaker: Story-Witch
dialogues.text: I brought you into being because I willed it so — just like the witch who created that evil dragon.

dialogues.speaker: Story-Witch
dialogues.text: But I promise you this: your birth was wanted, you are loved, and you will have a different fate than the dragon that came before you.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: You've never told me those things before, but for some reason, I always knew.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Thank you for... for bringing me into this world.

talks.objective: Discuss your experience within the story with Durin

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... Isn't this Mondstadt? Looks like we're back in the real world!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like there's more written on the page now, and less ink left than before. So, does that mean we've completed this chapter?

choices.text: So it is Durin's story, after all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, but why does "M" seem to think that the story isn't finished yet?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Durin broke free from the curse, came into this world with a new body, and even made a bunch of new friends. That already sounds like a happy ending to Paimon...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Maybe there'll be some clues in the following chapters?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: True... Everything's always so mysterious with these mages. Guess all we can do is wait for more clues.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: ...Huh.
Dodoco— Dodoco—
Is this thing on? Alright, that should do it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, that's Alice's voice!

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Hello there, children! If you're hearing this, you've stumbled upon the little recording I left for you. I thought you could use a few hints about how the book works.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: By now, I'm guessing you've already begun to leave your mark on the story. You should know, however, that the book needs time to absorb the ink — so the next chapter's clues won't show up right away.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, so... even magic ink needs time to dry!?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: The good news is, you can return to any chapter you've already completed, and continue to explore the mystical, magical storybook world YOU helped create!

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Have fun, dearies! Toodles!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aw, man. Paimon was so ready to knock this out in one go...

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Maybe it's for the best. Sooner or later, we'll end up being whisked off to another world again — and if that happens, who knows when we'll be able to come back.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: So it might be good to take a break while we can.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A break...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Guess now's as good a time as any...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, Paimon has a sudden craving for the Good Hunter's Sticky Honey Roast... And we happen to be in Mondstadt, so...

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: So... let's meet up here later? I need to find Miss Lisa to return those books, anyway.

choices.text: Or at least, a window into his past...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Experiment Log No. ■■■"

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Hm... This book definitely doesn't belong here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, we could tell just from reading the title...

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Albedo was the one who brought it in. He suggested I place it on the restricted list and keep it sealed away.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why?

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: He said it's full of forbidden alchemical formulas, some of which could even result in the creation of dangerous monsters.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Apparently, the danger it posed was so great, he didn't even feel like it was safe to carry around or keep it in his workshop.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: R—Really? Definitely sounds like it shouldn't be here, then...

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Still, if that mage read this book too... it must have been written a lot earlier than I'd imagined.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Second Strongest Spell in Existence..."

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Truly extraordinary... and certainly not the kind of thing that should be just lying around. In fact, Ms. Alice gave strict instructions about it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, it's some kind of book of spells? Paimon's guessing magic this powerful should be kept a secret...

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: It's true, this book does contain one of Ms. Alice's spells. But honestly, virtually no one could actually pull it off, even if they tried.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: The only reason it's even meant to be in the restricted section is because we can't let Klee get her hands on it.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: After Klee was born, Ms. Alice advised us to seal it away. She even added that little subtitle herself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So it's to keep it away from Klee, huh... Does that mean she could use it to cause even more mayhem than she already does with Jumpy Dumpty!?

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Haha, no, that's not it. As Ms. Alice herself put it, letting Klee see it too early would "spoil the surprise."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "■■ Verses"

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Yes... This is a restricted book alright. It certainly isn't supposed to be here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, but it looks like a regular poetry collection... How did it end up being classified as a restricted book?

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: The issue lies with one of the poems inside. You've heard of the great battle that took place on Dragonspine, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Five hundred years ago, during the cataclysm in Khaenri'ah, an evil dragon descended upon Mondstadt. A fierce battle with Dvalin ensued, but in the end, the evil dragon fell, and Dragonspine became its resting place.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: You're talking about Durin. The Durin of Dragonspine.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Well, the poem in question turns the whole battle into a dance, with the evil dragon recast as an innocent child who came here in search of friends...

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: But given all the suffering experienced at the claws of that dragon, how could the people of Mondstadt accept such a retelling?

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Bards are often accused of inventing history or distorting the truth in their ballads, but this one hit a bit too close to home...

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: And, since the Knights back then were unable to track down the author, they decided to ban the entire collection, blot out the title, and seal it away for good.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: So the version in the poem... It was all a lie?

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: ...I'm afraid that question is something only the dragon himself could answer.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Jumpy Dumpty Treasure Trove"

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Heh... Well, it definitely shouldn't be here, but I'd highly doubt it's one of the books you're looking for.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why's that?

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Because this is something Klee wrote. It's a compilation of all the best fish-blasting spots around Mondstadt, as well as the most convenient places to stash her new Jumpy Dumpties.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Of course, there's no way she'd get away with keeping a book like that in her bag, and she'd be in big, big trouble if Jean were to find out. Not only would the book itself be confiscated, but she'd be looking at a whole day in solitary confinement, at the very least.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Somehow, she figured out that the best place to hide it was right here. No place like a forest for hiding trees, huh? Now, every time it gets confiscated, she just writes a new one and sneaks it back in.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Guess it's a "restricted" book in its own way...

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Yes, haha — so thanks for helping me find it. I'll finally be able to hand it over to Jean.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "The Boar Princess"

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Well, this book has quite an obvious connection with that mage, considering she was the one who wrote it.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: But as one of the library's classics, its presence here is hardly unusual.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: It really is a must-read — so if you haven't read it yet, that's your homework, cutie.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This Dodoco doll is meant to be the witch in the story, right? Wait a second...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: All the people we've seen that looked like that turned out to be mages from the Hexenzirkel. D'you think the witch in this story is one of them too?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: My mother had a hat just like this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then, the witch must be "M"! Looks like this story really is about Durin, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Whether the sprite spoke true or not, it had little bearing on the story at hand.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: For in that moment, what mattered most was not that she was a witch, but a mother waiting for her child to hatch.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Hmm... Let's keep looking.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look at all these books. Guessing the witch did a lot of reading while she was waiting for the egg to hatch...

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: It just so happened, a dragon egg wasn't the only thing she was incubating here...

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Where else might a story be born, if not among books?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohhh...

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: For a moment, the story-crashers fell silent. Perhaps waiting around wasn't such a bad idea, after all?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Yet those who never stray beyond the main plot often miss the fun little details along the way...

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Clearly, both the golden-haired Traveler and the dragon-youth were eagerly awaiting the little dragon's birth. Though perhaps their longing burned a little too brightly?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Still, such fiery anticipation might itself become a blessing...

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Let every unborn life be welcomed with tender anticipation, and may that warmth stay with it for a lifetime.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: The day that the writer and the watcher crossed paths...

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: ...was the day that the magic known as storytelling was born.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Find the place I speak of, for it is where the seeds of this story lie.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: There, a witch once spent a sleepless night — and all to bring forth a story yet untold.
